qualification: One controlled HTTP-cache cold fill plus two same-selected-route warm attempts on one Chromium desktop runner; not a latency distribution or cold authentication/application/OS cache. Auth/IndexedDB/application stores were preserved; service-worker bypass was held for all reload samples.

All four usable endpoints attest selected active identity, six loaded/source messages, a visible known decrypted synthetic message, usable editor and available persisted snapshots of 23 chats/20 messages. This proves actual selected encrypted chat usability, not full fixture decryption or persistence of all seeded messages.

CPU is cumulative stable reported-process endpoint delta, includes automation/sampling and omits transient processes. Every reload has four stable processes and one reported replacement; RSS endpoints sum five reported processes and may double-count shared pages. No full CPU, peak/physical/page RAM claim.

ResourceTiming records actual selected-route transfer/encoded/decoded sizes, with 4096-entry capture installed, zero buffer-full/omitted counters and 436–462 entries. TAO/opaque/cache limitations remain. Zero observed .wasm-path resources does not establish zero embedded or differently named WASM.

Login automation to usable is 20299 ms, including fixture selection/readiness checks; shell readiness is 14257 ms. Reload usable endpoints include protocol/UI/assertion/runner work and are not pure transport latency, isolated KDF or WASM initialization.

The prior schemaVersion1 controlled checkpoint retained zero persisted messages and is historical shell/process evidence; its readiness numbers are not directly comparable to this stronger endpoint.
